jurisdictions.name: Grand Rapids / Kent County
notes: Grand Rapids requires a building permit for a pool or hot tub that can reach 24 inches of water depth or more.
The pool permit page asks for a pool installation plan and a site plan showing the pool location on the lot, uploaded with the application.
A non-owner applicant needs a Residential Builders License issued by the State of Michigan, or written authorization from a license holder.
The city points applicants to its Residential Pool Guide and its zoning rules for placement.

sources.title: Overview on Zoning and Permits for Home Renovation Projects
Residential Building Permits (City of Grand Rapids)

jurisdictions.name: Sterling Heights / Macomb County
jurisdictions.office: Office of Building, City of Sterling Heights
notes: Sterling Heights' pool guide covers pools and hot tubs with side walls over 24 inches. It lists a building permit application, plus electrical and mechanical permits where that work applies.
Pool plans must show the location on the property, with the water's edge at least 6 feet from side and rear lot lines and easements.
The plans must also show overhead wires, the electric meter and service line, barrier or enclosure details, and entrapment protection for a pool with a floor drain.
Inspections listed for an in-ground pool include a building open hole inspection and a final building inspection, with electrical inspections if electric is installed.

sources.title: Pool Permit Packet and Pool & Hot Tub Guide (Sterling Heights)

jurisdictions.name: Detroit / Wayne County
jurisdictions.office: Buildings, Safety Engineering and Environmental Department (BSEED)
notes: BSEED says building permits are applied for in the Accela portal, with scope of work and plans submitted through the ProjectDox portal.
BSEED's FAQ says single-family and duplex residential structures may apply in the office.
The Detroit Property Maintenance Code (Sec. 9-1-109) says pools must be fully enclosed by a fence at least 4 feet high with a self-latching gate.
The same section says pools must be installed consistent with the Michigan Construction Codes and have a working water filtration device.

sources.title: Detroit Property Maintenance Code, Chapter 9 (Sec. 9-1-109 Swimming pools)

jurisdictions.name: Ann Arbor / Washtenaw County
jurisdictions.office: Building, Rental and Inspection Services; Planning and Development Services
notes: Ann Arbor takes building permit applications through its STREAM online portal, which handles applications filed since March 2022.
Electrical, mechanical and plumbing trade permits are also applied for in STREAM and are not released until the related building permit is approved.
The city's accessory building handout lists pools among accessory structures. Zoning compliance permits for such structures must be submitted online in STREAM.

sources.title: Applications (Ann Arbor Building, Rental and Inspection Services)
Permits (Ann Arbor Building, Rental and Inspection Services)

jurisdictions.name: Rochester Hills / Oakland County
jurisdictions.office: City of Rochester Hills Building Department
notes: The city's pool guidebook says a building permit is required for a residential pool, hot tub or spa that has any one of these: a depth intended for swimming or bathing of more than 24 inches, a permanent water-recirculation system, or construction that involves structural materials. The construction documents are reviewed against the Michigan Residential Code and the International Swimming Pool and Spa Code.

The guidebook says pools, hot tubs and spas must be at least 5 feet from the side and rear property lines and 10 feet from the home, measured from the water's edge, and must not be located in any front yard.

The guidebook says the pool fence or barrier must be 48 inches above grade, measured on the side facing away from the pool, and pedestrian gates must open outward away from the pool and be self-closing with a self-latching device. A pool, hot tub or spa must not be filled with water until the Michigan Residential Code barrier requirements are completed.

The city's pool permit application guide lists the construction drawings for the pool as a required attachment. It also requires a site plan signed and sealed by a State of Michigan licensed design professional, and the completed City of Rochester Hills Pool Information Form. The guide says mechanical, electrical and plumbing permits can be applied for online after the building permit is issued.

sources.title: A Guide to Residential Swimming Pool, Hot Tub and Spa Construction (City of Rochester Hills, September 15, 2026)
Residential Swimming Pool, Hot Tub and Spa Permit Application Guide (City of Rochester Hills)
Apply for a Permit Online (City of Rochester Hills)

jurisdictions.name: Novi / Oakland County
jurisdictions.office: City of Novi Community Development Department
notes: The city's residential pool and spa sheet says a building permit is required for a pool or spa, and that all residential pools and spas must conform to the City of Novi Ordinance and comply with the 2015 International Swimming Pool and Spa Code. In-ground pools also need a Minor Land Improvement Permit. The sheet also requires a Woodland/Wetland Affidavit and asks for Homeowner Association or Architectural Control Committee approval, which can be the submitted plans with a signature and date.

Under its zoning requirements, the sheet says all pools must be at least 10 feet from the principal structure, but spas on decks or patios may be located anywhere within the approved deck requirements. Pools and spas cannot be within 10 feet of any overhead wires, and pools or spas must be no closer than 6 feet to any side or rear property line.

The sheet calls for an enclosure at least 4 feet high around the pool, with a gate that opens outward from the pool and is self-closing with a self-latching device. The same item lists an approved safety cover compliant with ASTM F-1346 as the other option. Spas or hot tubs may be equipped with a safety cover that complies with ASTM F 1346 instead of a barrier. In-ground pools need a construction safety fence during construction.

The sheet says the plan submittal shall include two sets of a site plan and pool plans. The site plan must show the pool's location in reference to property lines, the principal building and accessory structures, plus overhead power lines, fences and fence openings, the electrical and pump filter location, easements, and the well and septic location if applicable. In-ground pool plans must show the shape and size, materials, steel layout, electrical grounding, a sectional view showing depth and the location of the diving board, steps and ladder, the composition and width of the walking surface around the pool, and plumbing and heating.

sources.title: Residential Swimming Pool & Spa Requirements (City of Novi, July 19, 2024)
Information Requirements Sheets, Checklists, Manuals (City of Novi)
